page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance from the Dlsv6 series, configured with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio. It runs on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) and AVX-512 extensions. The instance is allocated 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It is a diskless instance containing no local NVMe storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities, and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong raw computational capabilities, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2042.0 and a multi-core score of 16898.0, alongside strong PassMark physics calculation performance. The memory subsystem records strong uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 205.24 GB/sec, while write operations and cached block access remain within median bounds. Hardware-accelerated matrix operations yield top-tier inference speeds for small language models, achieving 347.06 tokens per second on a 135M model. The trade-off of this architecture centers on its resource balance: the absence of integrated local scratch disks and the modest memory allocation per core restrict suitability for memory-intensive caching or heavy working-set applications.

By omitting high memory densities and local storage, the D32ls_v6 delivers qualitative cost efficiency for environments where CPU execution speed takes precedence over RAM capacity. The configuration fits compute-bound tasks that do not justify the cost of higher memory tiers. Typical suitable workloads include web serving fleets, with tested static web serving throughput reaching 55.94 GB/sec, along with continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, distributed microservices, and quantized CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, and is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM at 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong Geekbench single-core and multi-core performance, strong PassMark physics calculations, and robust uncached memory read bandwidth of 205.24 GB/sec. Built-in AMX and AVX-512 extensions provide high efficiency for lightweight AI inference tasks. With its reduced memory-to-core profile, the D32ls_v6 offers an economical deployment target for compute-bound workloads, batch processing, build automation, web application serving, and microservices architectures that do not require high memory density.
